description: Fixture for long text fields. `abstract` runs to a few hundred characters on the records that have one, so it should render as a full-width collapsible section rather than a key/value row; `title`, `author`, `journal`, `year` and `note` are short and must stay ordinary rows. One record's `note` is deliberately long — 1 of 12 — which must NOT move the whole column into an expander. One abstract carries embedded newlines, which must be treated as ordinary whitespace — the text reflows as a single paragraph rather than breaking there. The top-level `metadata` object exists to check that a wrapper object's entries are listed at the first level of the panel rather than costing an indentation layer.

records.title: Identification in models of intergenerational mobility
records.author: Grace Hopper
records.abstract: We study identification of intergenerational mobility parameters when the linkage between parents and children is incomplete and non-random. Existing approaches either discard unmatched records or impute them under assumptions that are difficult to defend. We show that the identified set for the rank-rank slope is characterized by a small number of moment inequalities, that it is sharp, and that it can be computed by linear programming. An application to administrative tax data narrows the reported range by roughly a third.

records.title: A note on facet counts
records.author: Ada Lovelace
records.abstract:
Faceted browsing is usually described informally. 

This note gives a precise statement of what a facet count should mean when several filters are active at once, and shows that the common implementation — recomputing every facet under all active filters — reports zero for values the user can still reach. 
The alternative excludes each field from its own facet.

records.title: Short one
records.author: Alan Turing
records.abstract: A brief remark on the same question, with no formal results.
records.note: This single note is deliberately much longer than the others, running well past the threshold on its own, to check that one outlier in an otherwise short column does not drag the whole column into an expander on every card in the dataset.

records.title: Sorting under incomplete information
records.author: John von Neumann
records.abstract: We consider a matching market in which one side observes only a coarse signal of the other side's type. The equilibrium exhibits partial assortativity: high types match assortatively among themselves while low types pool. Comparative statics in the precision of the signal are non-monotone, which we trace to a countervailing effect on the incentive to search.
